title: [Peek] Images do not size to fill the entire client area

judgment.rationale: Multiple dimensions and DPI scales reproduce consistent seams between the image and window chrome. The code path directly calculates a scaled requested size, clamps it, adds title-bar height, and centers the window, making this a focused fix candidate.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a shared Peek client-area sizing design, then validate both seam removal and the related centering examples from #50447.

evidence.fact: The report provides six image-size/display-scale examples with repeatable bottom or side gaps.
MainWindow.FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged performs scaling, monitor clamping, title-bar accounting, and CenterOnMonitor.
ImagePreviewer derives maximum image size from image dimensions and ScalingFactor.

fix_assessment.rationale: The symptom and affected code path are concrete, but no local fix has yet been validated across the reported DPI and aspect-ratio matrix.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Peek image-to-client sizing and centering
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The current path appears to mix scaled preview dimensions with window chrome/client dimensions, producing dimension-dependent gaps and offsets.
plan: Define one explicit unit contract for preview size, client size, and title-bar contribution.
Remove duplicate or inconsistent DPI/title-bar adjustments in FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged and its size event inputs.
Keep monitor-bound clamping and center the final window rectangle after the client size is finalized.
verification: Automated or manual matrix coverage reproduces the six examples from #50445 at 125% and 175%.
The #50447 small-image navigation video no longer changes centering based on image dimensions.
Window minimum-size and monitor-bound behavior remain intact.

confidence.rationale: The symptom maps directly to a small, identifiable Peek sizing path, but the intended native-versus-fit rule still needs confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Peek image previews leave repeatable gaps at the client-area edges across portrait, landscape, square, and very wide/tall images at 125% and 175% scaling.
known_information: The issue is open, assigned to daverayment, and labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, Product-Peek.
No diagnostic ZIP was attached; the report includes detailed dimensions, scales, and screenshots.
The same implementation path is implicated in #50447 centering offsets.
inferences: The likely defect is a mismatch among image pixel dimensions, DIPs, client-area dimensions, and title-bar accounting.
The existing TODO in the Peek sizing flow acknowledges portrait-image edge-to-edge problems.
issue_context.analysis: Normalize the sizing contract at the preview/window boundary and verify it with the exact reported matrix.

information_gaps.information: A maintainer-confirmed expected sizing rule for images smaller than, equal to, or larger than the available client area.
information_gaps.why_needed: The screenshots show the defect but do not fully define whether native pixels or a fit-to-client rule wins in every case.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the intended behavior in a follow-up comment, especially for portrait images and images smaller than the monitor client area.

comment.body: The report already supplies a strong matrix of image dimensions and 125%/175% display scales. Before implementation, please confirm the intended rule for images smaller than the available client area, including portrait images: should the preview preserve native pixels, fit the client area, or use a bounded hybrid rule? This distinction is needed to avoid removing seams by changing behavior that is intentionally native-sized.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Correct the Peek preview/window size contract so the image occupies the intended client area without double-applying DPI or title-bar dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: No reported image dimension leaves a seam at the client edge.
The 4K/175% centering examples from #50447 remain centered after navigation.
Portrait, landscape, square, and very wide/tall images pass at 125% and 175% scaling.
